# pbs_realm_sync (Action)

Syncs the users of an LDAP or Active Directory realm of a Proxmox Backup Server from its directory, as **Sync** under Configuration → Access Control → Realms does: PBS creates a user for every entry of the directory it takes for one — below `base_dn`, of one of `user_classes`, matching `filter` —, takes the names and email address of the users it has from the directory, and deletes the users it no longer finds as `remove_vanished` says. The users it creates have no privileges until a `pbs_acl` grants them some.

Needs `Permissions.Modify on /access/users`. The action first checks that the realm exists and is an LDAP or Active Directory realm: PBS would start the sync of a realm of another type, and fail it.

When it waits, the action reports how many users PBS created, updated and deleted, as the task's log names them — `dry_run` previews that without changing anything —, and warns about the entries of the directory PBS skipped.

~> **A sync changes users Terraform manages.** It overwrites the first name, last name and email address of the realm's users, `pbs_user` resources included, with the directory's — from the attributes the realm's `sync_attributes` names —, which the next plan shows as drift and reverts; with `properties` in `remove_vanished`, it also clears those the directory gives no valid value for, including those `sync_attributes` does not map: without `sync_attributes`, all three of every user it syncs. With `entry`, it deletes the realm's users the directory does not have, `pbs_user` resources included, with their API tokens — and with `acl` too, their ACL entries and their tokens': the next apply creates them again, the tokens with new secrets. A change of the realm's `base_dn`, `filter`, `user_classes` or `user_attr` changes which users a sync finds: preview what a sync with `entry` deletes then with `dry_run = true`. `enable_new = false` disables the users it finds that have no enabled flag stored in PBS, which includes the enabled users `pbs_user` creates (see `sync_defaults.enable_new` of `pbs_realm_ldap`). Manage the users of a realm either with `pbs_user` or by syncing, or give `pbs_user` the directory's values. Terraform orders the sync and the writes of users in the same run by their dependencies only: a user created in the same run may be synced, or deleted by `entry`, or not, depending on which comes first.

PBS refuses a second sync of a realm only while it is starting the first one: two syncs of the same realm can run at the same time, so trigger the action from one place.

-> Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later. OpenTofu and older Terraform releases do not support them, and Terraform 1.13 ignores `action` blocks without a word; set `required_version = ">= 1.14.1"` in configurations that use them. An action runs when a resource's `lifecycle` `action_trigger` fires, or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.<type>.<name>`, which also refreshes the state of the resources the action's configuration refers to, and of those they depend on, but of no other resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  # Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later; Terraform 1.13 would ignore them.
  required_version = ">= 1.14.1"
}

resource "pbs_realm_ldap" "corp" {
  realm     = "corp"
  server1   = "ldap.example.com"
  mode      = "ldaps"
  verify    = true
  base_dn   = "ou=people,dc=example,dc=com"
  user_attr = "uid"
  filter    = "(memberOf=cn=backup-users,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com)"

  bind_dn             = "uid=pbs,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com"
  password_wo         = var.bind_password
  password_wo_version = 1

  sync_attributes = {
    email     = "mail"
    firstname = "givenName"
    lastname  = "sn"
  }

  # Sync the users as soon as the realm exists, and whenever its settings
  # change.
  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.pbs_realm_sync.corp]
    }
  }
}

# Creates the users of the directory's group backup-users, disabled until an
# administrator enables them, and updates the names and email addresses of
# the users it has. It deletes nothing: with "entry", a change of base_dn,
# filter, user_classes or user_attr would delete, in the same apply, every
# user of the realm the new search no longer finds, with their API tokens.
action "pbs_realm_sync" "corp" {
  config {
    realm           = pbs_realm_ldap.corp.realm
    enable_new      = false
    remove_vanished = [] # removes nothing, whatever sync_defaults says
  }
}

# Also deletes the users of the realm that left the group, with their API
# tokens and ACL entries. Nothing triggers it: preview what it would delete
# with dry_run = true, then run it with
# terraform apply -invoke=action.pbs_realm_sync.corp_prune
action "pbs_realm_sync" "corp_prune" {
  config {
    realm           = pbs_realm_ldap.corp.realm
    enable_new      = false
    remove_vanished = ["entry", "acl"]
  }
}

variable "bind_password" {
  description = "Password of uid=pbs,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `realm` (String) Name of the LDAP or Active Directory realm, such as `pbs_realm_ldap.corp.realm`.

### Optional

- `dry_run` (Boolean) Whether only to find out what the sync would do: PBS logs the users it would create, update and delete, which the action reports, and saves nothing. Defaults to `false`.
- `enable_new` (Boolean) Whether the users the sync creates are enabled — and the users it updates that have no enabled flag stored in PBS, such as the enabled users `pbs_user` creates. Defaults to the realm's `sync_defaults.enable_new`, and to `true` when the realm sets none.
- `remove_vanished` (Set of String) What the sync removes that the directory no longer has, instead of what the realm's `sync_defaults.remove_vanished` says: `entry` the realm's users it does not find, with their API tokens; `acl`, together with `entry`, the ACL entries of those users and their tokens, and alone nothing; `properties` the first name, last name and email address of the users it finds that the directory gives no valid value for, including those the realm's `sync_attributes` does not map — so, for a realm without `sync_attributes`, all three of every user it syncs. Defaults to the realm's `sync_defaults.remove_vanished`, which removes nothing when the realm sets none. An empty set removes nothing, whatever the realm says.
- `timeout` (String) How long to wait for the PBS task, as a Go duration such as `90m` or `4h`. Defaults to the provider's `task_timeout`. When it runs out, the action fails, and the task goes on in PBS.
- `wait` (Boolean) Whether to wait for the PBS task to finish. Defaults to `true`: the action reports the task's progress, and fails when the task fails. With `false`, the action ends as soon as PBS has started the task, and the task's outcome is only in PBS (Administration → Tasks).
